findings.reason: the plan's own "does not add a third copy" intent is defeated if the consolidation lands beside the shared owner rather than inside it, and the author should place the routine in `discovery/base/` or justify why the base owner cannot serve SignalSource.
findings.text: §7 ("claim_sources_for_assignment" and "claim_sources_for_mapping" `workers.py:136,199` become one claim routine; `release_mapping_claim`/`release_mapping_claims_batch` `workers.py:274,287` become one release routine; the three `has_pending_*` checks `workers.py:303,329,343` become one pending check) is a census: every one of those seven helpers restates a claim/release/pending pattern the shared discovery layer already owns, via `claim_signal_sources` in `imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py:92` and `release_claim`/`release_claims_batch`/`reset_stale_claims`/`retry_on_deadlock` in `imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py`; the generalised routine belongs in the base owner (parameterised by status predicate, claim property names and returned fields, as §7 itself describes) so the other six claim families in `discovery/{paths,code,wiki,signals,mdsplus}` can converge on it, not in a fourth local variant in `ids/workers.py`

findings.reason: with the week's counts at 0/0/0/0 the section must, in its own text, account for the schema and public-definition surface it introduces, or state why none can be merged.
findings.text: §6 adds a `MAPPING_CANDIDATE` relationship, `candidate_status`/`candidate_route`/`candidate_claimed_at`/`candidate_claim_token`/`candidate_judged_at`/`candidate_model` on SignalSource, and the public functions `write_candidates` and `clear_candidates` in `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py`, and unlike §4 (which names the construction it moves and deletes), §5 (which states it retires nothing and why) and §7 (which names seven helpers collapsing to three and two `imas map run` options retiring in §8), it names neither what in these families it retires or merges nor why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §4/§5 place retrieval, pair judgment and routing behind one module, `imas_codex/ids/candidates.py`, with `retrieve_candidates`, `judge_candidates` and `route` hiding the shortlist, the LLM call and the threshold logic; §7 consolidates seven claim helpers into three rather than adding a fourth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 generalises the SignalSource claim pattern inside `imas_codex/ids/workers.py:136,199,274,287,303,329,343`, but that pattern is already owned by the shared discovery layer (`imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py:92 claim_signal_sources`; `imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py` `retry_on_deadlock`, `release_claim`, `release_claims_batch`, `reset_stale_claims`), which the plan does not extend or name.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6 adds a schema relationship, six SignalSource fields and two public functions without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §4 re-points the shortlist construction at `hybrid_dd_search` (`imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:97`), `cluster_search` (`dd_search.py:869`, which does support the path-lookup branch `ClusterSearcher.search_by_path` relied on today), `analyze_units` (`imas_codex/ids/tools.py:168`) and `fetch_cross_facility_mappings` (`tools.py:733`), and §5 reuses the §25 decisions layer rather than writing a client.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the new `candidates.py` is a *move* of the construction already at `imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:781–820` into a shared owner that `gather_ids_context` then calls, and §4 states why the maintained search owners cannot be widened (`hybrid_dd_search` signature frozen) instead of forking them.
